notes: DECISIONS TAB (new) plus TWO CORRECTNESS FIXES found by replaying real user data. BUG 1 — ONE-OFF CONTAMINATION OF THE CASHFLOW AND COVER TESTS (severe, produced wildly wrong verdicts). The emergency-cover floor was computed as floorMonths x totalExpense[i], but totalExpense includes LUMPY one-off items: a backdrop scenario's down payment, a holiday, an upfront child cost, the candidate purchase's own deposit. On a real dataset this made April 2027 report a 'monthly outflow' of Rs 9,40,760 and therefore demanded a six-month floor of Rs 56,44,558, against Rs 1,82,063 of cash. The same contamination hit the buffer and EMI-vs-spare-cash tests, which saw a monthly surplus of minus Rs 6,76,760. Result: a perfectly serviceable Rs 14.42L car was reported as first affordable in late 2030 instead of 2028. FIX: lumpy items are now identified structurally — any scenario row non-zero in at most two months of the horizon is a lump, not a commitment — and stripped from all three cashflow tests, which measure the capacity to service an EMI month after month. They are judged solely by the liquidity test, which asks whether enough cash survives them. The structural test is label-independent, so it stays correct however a scenario names its rows, and it automatically catches the candidate's own deposit because the candidate is itself modelled as a scenario. Verified: earliest feasible moved from 2030-11 to 2028-07 on the same inputs. BUG 2 — LIQUIDITY DEFINED INCONSISTENTLY WITH THE REST OF THE APP. The cover test counted cash only, while the Dashboard's liquidity health counts cash plus any investment flagged liquid. The same purchase could therefore look affordable on the Dashboard and blocked on Decisions. Decisions now uses the Dashboard's definition. (No numeric change on datasets where every instrument is flagged illiquid, but the two pages can no longer disagree.) EARLIER IN THE SAME BUILD, two further modelling bugs were found and fixed: the candidate's own deposit was being treated as recurring cashflow (now a balance-sheet event, superseded by the general fix above); and the affordability search held an absolute deposit fixed while shrinking the price, so a liquidity block could never be relieved and the search returned Rs 0 however cheap the item became — the deposit now scales with the price, which also restores the monotonicity the binary search depends on. Where no price clears, the page now names what is actually binding instead of quoting a meaningless Rs 0. WHAT THE TAB DOES: a SCENARIO is an assumed change to the world; a DECISION is a question being answered, tested against the enabled scenarios as backdrop, which is listed explicitly on the page. It answers three things: can I at this month; when can I, with the blocking constraint named and the month it lifts; and how much can I spend at a given month. FOUR TESTS, each measured at its own worst month across the full tenure: EMI vs income, EMI vs pre-EMI spare cash, money left over, and liquid assets vs an N-month cover floor. THREE APPETITES: Comfortable 15/50/Rs 15,000/6mo, Balanced 20/62/Rs 10,000/4.5mo, Aggressive 26/78/Rs 5,000/3mo. Tightest binds. IMPLEMENTATION: no new engine maths. A candidate is expressed as a synthetic house-type scenario and passed to runProjection(), inheriting salary growth, expense inflation, EMI schedules and every enabled scenario. runProjection is untouched, as is the v2026.05.05.15 live-anchored EOM savings fix. IMPORTANT USAGE NOTE: enabled scenarios are the backdrop, so an enabled 'Car Purchase' scenario means a car decision is judged in a world where a car has ALREADY been bought — two deposits and two EMIs. On the real dataset this alone moved the earliest feasible date from 2027-11 to 2028-05. Disable a scenario before asking the same question as a decision. HONESTY NOTE SHOWN IN-APP: the engine books a house or land purchase as money out but does not add the property to assets, so the net-worth cost shown overstates the true cost by the equity being built. The page prices a decision; it does not claim to say whether to make it. PERFORMANCE: one runProjection is ~20ms over a ten-year horizon. Every search is hard-bounded by DC_LIMITS (96-month sweep, 6-month stride, 20 coarse probes, 6 fine, 12 bisection iterations); no loop can run unbounded on any input. Measured on real data: single evaluation ~27ms, full sweep ~350ms, affordability search ~190ms. ROBUSTNESS: detail rendering uses a monotonic token, so switching decisions mid-run is never dropped and a stale run cannot overwrite the panel on screen. The save path no longer reassigns state.decisions unconditionally, which would have discarded saved decisions if state were ever mid-reload. SCHEMA v16 adds state.decisions; freshState() seeds it too, so new and migrated users both get it. SCOPE: purely additive apart from APP_VERSION and the schema-version line. Scenarios, Dashboard, Budget, Journal, Projection, Net Worth, Instruments, EMI Calculator, Rates and Edit-my-inputs are unchanged and were re-run clean. TO VERIFY: hard-refresh, confirm v2026.05.06.02, open Decisions, add a purchase, press 'Work it through'. Check the Backdrop card lists your enabled scenarios and that toggling one changes the verdict.
